After that, “Yuvarlat” and “Pah kır” follow one clean edge, “Yüzey sil” takes away a whole rounding or the wall of a hole, and a STEP export carries the real faces. The status line says what was found, such as "planes: 9, cylinders: 4".

What fits none of these surfaces stays as small flat facets, and the message says how much of the surface that is. A body that is mostly free-form, such as a figure or a sculpted shape, stays a mesh, and so does a mesh with gaps or crossed walls, which cannot close into a solid. Up to 400,000 triangles are taken, and a large mesh can take a few minutes. A larger mesh goes below that with “Ağı sadeleştir” and “Keep edges and holes” switched on; otherwise take the mesh as it came, it comes out cleanest. One undo step brings the mesh back.

For a small mesh with round faces, up to 4,000 triangles, the edge tools do this by themselves: rounding an edge of such an STL rebuilds it the same way first.

Reporting a bug

If layerling does something unexpected, save a “Hata raporu”: the link sits in the footer at the bottom, next to the forum. It is a ZIP file, because GitHub and many forums refuse a bare .lyl: inside are your design as a .lyl and a short text file with the version, browser, screen size, the last messages and any errors. The start page opens the ZIP like a backup, or you unpack it and open the .lyl. Nothing personal is in it. Attach the file to your post in the forum or on GitHub, so the problem can be followed with exactly your design.

If layerling stops with an error, a window with the error message shows instead of a blank page. From it you can save the state of the design last stored in the browser as a .lyl file, go back to the overview, or start a new design. The error message from the window and the saved file help when you report it.

Shared designs on a server

When layerling runs on your own computer or web server, it can offer a shared folder in which all users keep designs. The start page then holds the designs in two tabs, “Sunucu” for the shared folder and one for this browser, each with the number of designs in it; the one with more designs comes first and is open. You create folders there, move designs by dragging and search across the whole folder. A design that lives there saves itself back to it. A design from this browser goes onto the server by dragging its card onto the “Sunucu” tab, or with “Sunucuya koy” in the card's menu. While the “Sunucu” tab is open, “Yeni 3D tasarım oluştur” and “Yedeği geri yükle” put the design into the server folder you have open, and “Tümünü yedekle” packs every design of the server, in its folders, and its custom shapes into one ZIP file. The start page shows a design by its file name, so renaming a design, on its card or at the top of the editor, renames the file on the server too. Deleting a design or a folder removes it for good, together with its working copy in this browser. Custom shapes kept on the server sit in its folder Custom shapes, see Shapes.

Two things make that quicker: “Tümünü sunucuya koy” on the start page puts every design of this browser on the server in one go, and ticking “Yeni tasarımlar sunucuda” makes every new design start in the server folder, so it is saved there from the first change on. With the tick, everything else that makes a design starts there too: opening or importing a file, “Yedeği geri yükle” (with the backup's folders), duplicating and taking a state from the history, each into the server folder you had open; “Yeni klasör” on the start page then makes a folder on the server. A design made in the first moments waits until the server has answered. When new designs must always start on the server and this browser holds none of its own, the start page shows only the server's designs. The tick is kept in this browser. A design that cannot go - its name is taken on the server, say - stays in the browser, and the message says how many.

The other export formats (STL, 3MF, OBJ, STEP, SVG, PNG and the drawing) can go into the same folder: in the export window, “Sunucuya kaydet” writes the file next to your design, or into the folder you have open on the start page for a design that is not on the server. A program that shares the folder, such as a slicer in Docker, can open it from there. The file does not appear in the list of designs. If a file of that name is already there, the message says so, and pressing the button again replaces it.

That is not simultaneous editing: whoever opens a file works on a copy of their own. If somebody else has changed the file in the meantime, layerling refuses to overwrite it.

On layerling.com this function is not switched on. How to set it up on your own server is described in the README on GitHub.

13. Keyboard shortcuts

All keys at a glance, taken straight from the program so the list is always right.

Bu bölüm henüz Türkçeye çevrilmedi. Aşağıda İngilizce metin var.

The shortcuts work as long as the workplane has the focus. While you type in a field they keep out of the way. On the Mac, Cmd applies wherever Ctrl is listed here.

In the editor, “Klavye kısayolları” in the “Yardım” area opens the same list as a window. The printer button in the window (“Listeyi yazdır veya PDF olarak kaydet”) prints the list on its own, black on white, the whole list on one side of an A4 or Letter sheet in three columns, to keep at hand as a quick reference; the print dialog of the browser also offers to save it as a PDF.

The box at the top of the window searches the list: it keeps only the shortcuts whose sentence, group or keys contain every word you type, so "fillet" or "ctrl+z" leaves just those rows. Capital letters and accents do not matter, and a single letter or digit finds that key and the words that start with it. The X at the end of the box empties it; with the box empty the whole list is back. The printer button prints what the window shows, so after a search it prints only the shortcuts found.

Command search

Can't find a tool? Press Ctrl+K or click the magnifying glass in the “Yardım” area, then type what you are looking for: a tool ("fillet", "mirror"), a shape ("cylinder") or a command ("export", "undo"). Move with the arrow keys and press Enter, or click the entry.

  • The search understands the English and the German word alike and ignores capital letters and umlauts: "aushoehlen" finds “İçini boşalt”.
  • Every entry shows the keys that do the same and the group of the ribbon it lives in, so you learn where it is.
  • Entries that are greyed out cannot run right now, mostly because nothing is selected. They stay in the list so the search still tells you where the tool is.

The guide you are reading has a search box too, at the top of every page: type a word or two and it lists the sections that contain all of them, with the matching words marked. Click one, or press Enter for the first, to jump straight there. The page it opens marks every place your words appear and scrolls to the first one in that section; Esc or a click on a mark clears them.

  • A shape's name adds that shape to the workplane, just like clicking it in the shapes menu.
  • With an empty field the search lists the commands you used last at the top.
  • The name of a body in your design finds that body and selects it, which helps in a design with many parts. Bodies only appear once you type.
  • A custom shape you saved is found by its name too, once you type, and a click puts it into the design as in the shapes panel.
  • It works in sketch mode as well, with the sketch tools.

Your own keys

Any command of the command search can go on a key of your own: a tool you use all the time, a shape, “Çalışma düzleminde ortala” or “Open the shapes panel”.

  1. Open “Klavye kısayolları” and click “Add a key” under “Your own keys” at the top of the window.
  2. Type a few letters of the command and click it, or press Enter for the first one.
  3. Press the key you want, alone or with Ctrl, Alt or Shift. Letters, digits and F1 to F12 can take a command.

A key the editor already uses, one the browser keeps for itself (such as Ctrl+W) or one of your own keys is refused, and the window says what it does. Click a key in the list to change it, the X next to it to remove it, or “Remove all my keys” to start over.

  • The key runs the command just as the command search does. If it cannot run right now, mostly because nothing is selected, the status bar says so.
  • Your keys show next to their commands in the command search and on the printed list.
  • They stay in this browser, like the theme. A key for a sketch tool works in sketch mode, a key for the 3D editor outside it.
  • While you type in a field, your keys keep out of the way like all the others.

Interactive Help

Cannot find where to read about a button or a field? Let the program take you there. Click the question mark in the “Yardım” area, or press Shift+F1. The pointer turns into a question mark, and whatever lies under it is outlined.

  • Click a button, a field, a switch, a handle, a group of the ribbon or the title bar of a window. It does not do what it normally does. A small window opens instead, with the name of the element, a short summary of the part of this guide that is about it, up to two more places that mention it, and “Kılavuzda aç”.
  • The help is about the element you pointed at, not about the whole window around it. An element without a name of its own uses the nearest one around it; inside a window it falls back on that window's question mark.
  • “Kılavuzda aç” opens the guide at that section in a new tab. There the section is outlined in colour, from its heading to its end, so you see where it starts and stops.
  • If the guide says nothing about the element, the window says so and offers “Kılavuzda ara”.
  • Esc, or the question mark again, leaves the mode. On a touch screen there is no hover: a tap on an element opens the window straight away.

The window moves by its title bar like the other windows. The program finds the section by the name of the element - the label on a button, the name of a field - because this guide writes every button as it is called in the program. It looks it up in the same search as the box at the top of each guide page, in the language you are using, and runs entirely in your browser.

14. Building with an AI (MCP)

How an AI assistant such as Gemini, Claude or Codex creates and changes shapes, groups them and takes pictures of the view in your open editor.

Bu bölüm henüz Türkçeye çevrilmedi. Aşağıda İngilizce metin var.

layerling comes with an MCP server. MCP is a standard through which an AI assistant can use tools in other programs. With it an AI client such as Gemini, Claude or Codex sees an open editor tab and works in it: it creates shapes, changes dimensions, groups, cuts, rounds edges, reads out the scene and takes pictures of the view. You describe the part, the AI builds it, you watch and can step in at any moment.

The bridge between AI client and editor runs locally on your computer. Keep in mind, though: what the AI reads, meaning the scene and the pictures of the view, goes to the provider of your AI client, like any other input there.

Important: The MCP bridge exists in the development server that you start yourself on your computer. On layerling.com and in installations with static hosting it is switched off. A copy you host yourself, such as the Docker image on a NAS, can switch it on with an access token; see "A copy on a NAS or server" below.

Step by step for beginners

You do not need to know anything about programming for this.

The shortest way: give your favourite AI the address of the project, https://github.com/henmedia/layerling, and ask it: "Set up layerling on my computer so that I can build 3D models with you through its MCP server." It downloads and installs everything itself and tells you when it is done. This works with an AI that can work on your computer, such as the Code tab of the Claude app, Codex, Antigravity or Gemini CLI. A chat in the browser cannot do it, because it cannot install anything on your computer.

Or do it yourself, on Windows with the Claude app, in five steps:

1. Install layerling. Open the Start menu, type PowerShell and open Windows PowerShell. Copy this line, paste it into the window with a right-click and press Enter:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/henmedia/layerling/main/scripts/windows-quickstart.ps1 | iex

It installs what layerling needs, downloads layerling into the folder layerling in your user folder (C:\Users\<your name>\layerling) and opens it in your browser. The first time this takes a few minutes.

2. Keep layerling running. layerling runs as long as the PowerShell window stays open, and the AI can only build while it runs. Next time, double-click "Start layerling" on your desktop instead.

3. Install the Claude app. Install the Claude app for Windows and sign in. The Code tab used in the next step is part of the paid Claude plans.

4. Open the layerling folder in the Code tab. In the Claude app, switch to Code at the top and choose the folder layerling in your user folder as the folder to work in. layerling already brings everything Claude needs to find its tools. If Claude asks whether it may use the MCP server "layerling" of this folder, allow it.

5. Tell Claude what to build. For example: "Use the layerling tools and build me a round box, 60 mm across and 40 mm high, with a 2.5 mm wall." If no editor is open, Claude opens one in your browser, builds the box there step by step and takes pictures to check its work. You watch and can change anything yourself at any time.

On a Mac it goes the same way, with these changes. In step 1, open the Terminal app (press Cmd+Space, type Terminal and press Enter), paste this line and press Enter:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/henmedia/layerling/main/scripts/mac-quickstart.sh | sh

If Git or Node.js is missing, it tells you what to install (macOS offers Git in a window, Node.js comes as an installer from nodejs.org); afterwards run the same line again. In step 2, the shortcut on your desktop is also called "Start layerling". In step 3, install the Claude app for Mac.

Tip: If something does not work, tell Claude what you see. It can read the error and usually fixes it itself. If nothing happens in the editor, check first that layerling is still running (step 2).

Setting up

  1. Get layerling from GitHub and start it in the project folder with npm run dev. Node.js must be installed. On Windows the quick-start line in the README takes care of that.
  2. Open an editor tab, for example http://127.0.0.1:3000/?editor=1. You can leave that to the AI: when no editor is open, the first tool that needs one starts your browser with an editor and waits until it has connected. That works for a layerling on your own computer; a copy on a NAS or server needs you to open the editor. Set LAYERLING_MCP_OPEN_EDITOR=0 for the MCP server to switch it off.
  3. Connect your AI client to the MCP server. The client starts it itself with node scripts/layerling-mcp-server.mjs.

Claude Code

Nothing to install: the project brings a .mcp.json that registers the server, and the skill under .claude/skills/layerling-mcp-skill. Open the layerling folder in Claude Code and ask, for example: "Use the layerling MCP tools to list my open editors and inspect the scene."

Claude Desktop

Claude Desktop does not read project files. Enter the server in its own configuration. As a template use docs/mcp/claude-desktop-config.example.json in the project, replacing the script path with the absolute path on your computer. Then restart Claude Desktop.

Codex

Copy the skill from docs/skills/layerling-mcp-skill into your Codex skills folder, enter the server in your Codex configuration using docs/mcp/codex-config.example.toml, and restart Codex.

Gemini & Antigravity

Antigravity auto-discovers the workspace skill in .agents/skills/layerling-mcp-skill. For Gemini CLI, copy the skill from docs/skills/layerling-mcp-skill into your global skills folder (~/.gemini/skills/), add the server to your settings using docs/mcp/gemini-config.example.json, and restart the client.

The detailed instructions for each client are in the README on GitHub.

A copy on a NAS or server

A copy you host yourself can let an AI client drive its open editors over the network. It is off by default, because whoever can drive the bridge can read and change the open designs. On the server, set LAYERLING_MCP_REMOTE to true and LAYERLING_MCP_TOKEN to a secret of at least 16 characters (for the Docker image in environment: of the compose file; no rebuild needed). Open an editor tab of that copy and keep it open, and give the MCP client the address and the same token: LAYERLING_URL=http://nas:3000 and LAYERLING_MCP_TOKEN=<the token>.

Only a client with the token can list or drive the editors. The editor pages need none, but they only count under an address or name that only your own network can use (an IP address, a name without a dot, or one ending in .local or .lan); a real domain behind a reverse proxy goes into LAYERLING_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Use it on a network you trust, and HTTPS beyond it. The README has the details.

What the AI can do

The AI works with the same functions as you, through the same path as your operation in the editor. New layerling functions get their MCP action right away. The tools:

ToolWhat it does
layerling_list_editorslists the open editor tabs
layerling_rename_projectgives the project a name, as the pencil beside the project name does
layerling_open_editoropens a new editor tab in your default browser and waits until it has connected (on your own computer only)
layerling_read_scenereads scene, selection, units and the exact dimensions of all objects
layerling_list_objectslists all objects with dimensions, position, rotation and id
layerling_select_objectsselects objects
layerling_hide_othershides everything but the selection or the given objects, in one undo step
layerling_delete_objectsdeletes objects
layerling_move_objectmoves an object to another place in the object list
layerling_create_shapecreates a shape: box, cylinder, text (also curved), thread, gear, sketch body and all the others
layerling_import_fileimports a file as the import window does, a coloured OBJ or 3MF as one body per colour, a 3MF with several objects as one body per object
layerling_add_fontadds a font of one's own for text from a TrueType, OpenType or WOFF file; it stays in the browser, a design keeps only the letters it uses
layerling_list_fontslists the built-in fonts and the fonts of one's own, with id and name
layerling_import_meshbrings a triangle mesh into the design
layerling_update_objectchanges dimensions, position, colour, name, solid or hole and everything else that makes up the shape, a text's letter edge included
layerling_align_objectsaligns objects with each other
layerling_scale_objectsscales objects by a percentage, together or each in place
layerling_lay_flatlays an object with one face on the plate
layerling_place_on_facesets objects down on a face of another, sloped ones too, like the C key
layerling_perforate_facecuts a hole pattern into a flat face or round the wall of a cylinder, tube or bore; the holes stay as holes grouped with the body
layerling_sweep_sketchpulls a rectangular or round cross-section along a path of points as one exact body; a closed path makes a ring
layerling_push_facepushes a flat face out or cuts a pocket into it, with an inset from the edge and a corner radius; the new part is a sketch body grouped with the body, or a free body of its own with separate
layerling_paintpaints parts of a body in colours of their own for printing in several colours (Paint): fill a face up to its sharp edges, a round patch, or a lasso drawn in a flat view; erase, clear; saved with the body and written to a 3MF as painted faces
layerling_support_ribstands a thin support rib under the lower face of a part printed tilted on one edge, with bridges one layer high (Support rib)
layerling_stencil_bridgesholds the parts of a plate with text cut through that would fall out, with bridges grouped with the plate, as wide and high as set (Stencil bridges)
layerling_mate_facesbrings a face of one object against a face of another, face to face or flush, or puts two round faces on one axis
layerling_open_groupopens a group so its parts can be changed one by one, also a group inside an open one
layerling_close_groupcloses it again ("Done") or cancels
layerling_add_to_groupputs loose objects into a group without opening it
layerling_take_out_of_grouptakes one part out of a group without opening it
layerling_group_objectsgroups objects
layerling_ungroup_objectsdissolves groups
layerling_boolean_cutcuts solids with holes
layerling_intersect_objectskeeps only what the objects have in common (Intersection)
layerling_hull_objectswraps the objects in one convex body, as if shrink-wrapped (Hull)
layerling_cookie_cuttermakes a cookie cutter from the objects: a wall with a cutting edge and a rim round the mirrored outline (Cookie cutter)
layerling_flexi_jointscuts a flat body into links with joints printed in place that swing to the sides (Flexi joints)
layerling_make_lidmakes a lid for a body open at the top: pushed in, over the top or flat, with the fit you choose and magnets if you like (Lid)
layerling_make_cable_channelruns a round channel for a cable through a body from an entry to an exit, finding the way itself with gentle bends (Cable channel)
layerling_loft_sketchesjoins two sketch bodies into a loft from one outline to the other (Loft sketches)
layerling_separate_partsseparates a shape into its loose parts, a sketch body into one body per outline
layerling_split_objectscuts solids or holes in two with a plane
layerling_list_edgeslists the real CAD edges of an object
layerling_apply_edge_treatmentchamfers or fillets chosen edges
layerling_hollow_objecthollows a body with an even wall
layerling_cut_outcuts one solid out of another so they fit: the part stays, a copy grown by the clearance is subtracted from the other body
layerling_punchpunches the outline of one solid, seen along x, y or z, straight through another; the punch stays and need not touch it
layerling_offset_objectbuilds the clearance of a press fit: grows or shrinks a solid, or adds the grown copy as a hole, or moves only the sides
layerling_list_faceslists the faces of an exact body
layerling_delete_facesdeletes faces and closes the gap
layerling_array_objectsmultiplies in a row, in a grid or on a circle
layerling_bundle_objectsbundles objects like Ctrl+B: they move together, keep their colour and kind and go out separately in an export
layerling_layer_textturns a text into a stack of layers for a multicolour print (letters, wider rims, a plate without holes) or builds a stack again, with a key ring hole, the corners per layer and a rounded or chamfered letter edge; with a name list, one tag per name
layerling_text_blockmakes a text block: a text becomes the first of several lines, each a text of its own under the one above, aligned left, centred or right, each line the same size or smaller
layerling_layer_iconturns an SVG icon (the text of the file, or an extruded sketch body) into a layered icon tag for a multicolour print - the icon, wider rims, a plate without holes - or builds one again with a new width or layers; with a count it fills the plate with copies
layerling_create_qr_codemakes a QR code from a text or web address, like “QR kod” in the shape library - the code alone, raised on a plate or engraved, with error correction, width, height, quiet zone and as a hole if asked; it warns when a module gets under 0.8 mm
layerling_create_sbc_boardplaces an SBC board true to size, like “SBC kartı” in the shape library - Raspberry Pi 5, 4, 3 B+, Zero 2 W or BIGTREETECH Pi, with its holes and connectors, the clearance round the edge connectors, the position and as a hole to cut a case
layerling_reference_imageadds a reference image from a picture, as “Referans görseli” does, or moves, turns, calibrates (two points of the picture and their real distance), fades or locks one - a guide that is never exported or printed; trace turns its dark or light part into a sketch body standing on it
layerling_measure_sectionmeasures on a cutting plane between two points that snap to the outline - wall thickness, gaps, fits
layerling_show_overhangsswitches the overhang hatching on or off, sets the angle and reports for each body the area that would need supports
layerling_estimate_printestimates volume, weight and filament for the selection or the whole design: for a solid body, and as a rough guess with walls and infill like the export window
layerling_check_clearancechecks before printing which parts overlap, touch or come closer than a minimum gap (Check clearance), the separate parts of one object too
layerling_printer_playreads, sets or clears the printer's play (“Printer play” in the settings) and places the fit test that measures it
layerling_check_printchecks before printing what would go wrong: walls too thin for the nozzle, floating parts, small contact with the plate, overhangs and open meshes (Print check)
layerling_add_reference_pointsmarks reference points - on the centre, corners or edge middles of objects, or at exact positions - that shapes snap to
layerling_list_reference_pointslists the reference points with their ids and positions
layerling_remove_reference_pointsdeletes reference points by id, or all of them
layerling_list_notesreads the user's notes with their text, the body each is pinned to and whether it is a request for the AI
layerling_wait_for_noteswaits until you tick “For the AI” on a note, and hands the request over at once
layerling_add_noteputs a note on the model, pinned to an object or free on the plate
layerling_update_notechanges a note or answers it; an answer closes the request
layerling_remove_notesdeletes notes by id
layerling_inspect_errorsshows the last message and the last error, plus the messages and errors of the session
layerling_wrap_around_cylinderwraps a body lying flat, an SVG or text for example, around a cylinder, outward or inward as an engraving
layerling_texture_surfacelays a surface texture onto a body: grooves, knurling, honeycomb or bumps, for grip or for looks, and changes or removes it later
layerling_simplify_meshreduces the triangle count of an imported mesh, to a share in percent or to a number of triangles
layerling_make_exactturns an imported mesh into an exact CAD body: planes, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori become real faces, so edges round cleanly and STEP carries them
layerling_save_custom_shapekeeps bodies as a custom shape, on the server or in the browser, to insert them into other designs
layerling_list_custom_shapeslists the custom shapes on the server and in the browser
layerling_insert_custom_shapeinserts a custom shape into the open design, at a spot x/z if you like
layerling_delete_custom_shaperemoves a custom shape; inserted bodies stay
layerling_show_workplanehides and shows the plate with its grid, for a picture of the underside for example (only the view)
layerling_set_section_viewcuts the view open along a plane to look inside (only the view, nothing is cut apart)
layerling_measurementsshows or hides the measurements of the tape measure and lists them with their lengths, hides or shows the sizes around the selection like Q, and types a length for one of them, which moves the body at its end like a click on its number
layerling_measure_anglemeasures an angle like the protractor: at the corner of three points or between two flat faces, and shows it in the view
layerling_saved_viewsaves the current view under the key 7, 8, 9 or 0 and goes back to it, like Shift+key and the key (only the view); also sets the start view of new designs
layerling_build_plateslists, adds, names, orders and removes the build plates, moves objects onto a plate and arranges them on the plates, like the plate bar
layerling_clear_historydeletes every undo step for good, as the History view's "Delete history" button does; needs confirm: true
layerling_set_history_viewlooks back at an earlier state of the project, like the History view (the real design stays untouched; changing tools wait until it is closed)
layerling_restore_from_historybrings objects (also parts inside groups) back from an earlier state into the design as copies, as the History view's Bring into design does - one step that undo takes back
layerling_export_section_svgreturns the outlines on a cutting plane as an SVG at 1:1, from the same bodies as the export
layerling_sketch_from_sectionmakes a sketch from the outlines on a cutting plane, lying on the cut: opened in the editor to change, or built at once into a body of a given height
layerling_export_drawingmakes the workshop drawing of the "2D" export: three views at 1:1 on an ISO sheet with overall sizes and a table of the round bores, as SVG text or PDF
layerling_export_meshwrites the file of the export window as STL, 3MF, OBJ, SVG (top view, footprint or visible edges) or DXF for laser cutting, from the same bodies; to a path on this computer, or as base64
layerling_save_projectsaves the whole editable design as a .lyl file at a path on the computer where the MCP server runs, without a dialog; an existing file is only replaced with overwrite, it is written through a temporary file, and the target of Ctrl+S in the editor stays as it is
layerling_list_attachmentslists the files attached to the design (name, type, size), as the Attachments panel shows them
layerling_get_attachmentreads one attached file, its bytes as base64, as Download in the panel does
layerling_add_attachmentattaches a file given as base64, with the panel's checks; a name already attached is only overwritten with replace
layerling_rename_attachmentgives an attached file another name; its content stays
layerling_remove_attachmentremoves an attached file for good; needs confirm: true
layerling_set_workplaneputs the workplane on a side of a body or back on the base plate, and hides or shows it
layerling_capture_imagetakes a picture of the view: front, top, side, diagonally from a corner and more

That lets the AI check itself: it creates something, takes a picture, looks and improves.

An example

You say: "Build me a round box 60 mm across, 40 mm high with a 2.5 mm wall, open at the top, plus a flat lid with 'Tea' written in an arc." The AI creates the cylinders, hollows one, puts the curved text on the lid and takes pictures at the end to see whether it fits.

Tip: Give the AI concrete dimensions and tell it what the part is for ("holder for a 12 mm rod, fits a Bambu Lab A1"). Then it makes more sensible decisions. And watch it build: you can step in yourself at any time, because it is the same editor.

15. Installing as an app, working offline and self-hosting

Start layerling like a normal program, even without a network, and how to run it on your own computer.

Bu bölüm henüz Türkçeye çevrilmedi. Aşağıda İngilizce metin var.

Installing as an app

layerling can be installed like a normal program. It then gets an icon and a window of its own, without an address bar. After the first visit it starts even without internet. Your designs stay on your computer. Installing is worth it: the app starts faster, because it does not have to be loaded again each time, it works without internet and it spares the server. You lose nothing, as layerling still tells you when a new version is out. This also protects your designs: Safari on the Mac and on iPhone and iPad clears the stored data of a website that has not been visited for seven days, but not that of an installed app.

On the start page a hint with “Şimdi yükle” appears if your browser can do it. Otherwise:

  • Chrome and Edge: Click the install icon at the right of the address bar, or choose "Install as app" in the browser menu.
  • Safari on the Mac: Menu "File", then "Add to Dock".
  • Safari on iPhone and iPad: Share icon, then "Add to Home Screen".
  • Firefox: cannot install apps. layerling still starts offline in a tab there.

You can close the hint on the start page with “Bu ipucunu gizle”. Starting the installed app a second time in Chrome or Edge brings the open window to the front instead of opening another one.

On a computer, an installed layerling in Chrome or Edge also registers as a program for .lyl files: a double click on a design in the file manager opens it in layerling, and Ctrl+S saves back into that file. It does the same for .stl and .3mf files, which open as a new design, as with “Tasarım aç veya geometri içe aktar” on the start page. To make layerling the default for them, choose it under Open with and let the system always use it. On Android this does not work, there the browser offers no file association for installed web apps; open a design with “Tasarım aç veya geometri içe aktar” on the start page.

Updates

When a newer version exists, layerling shows it on the start page. Through “Sürüm notları ve indirme” you read what has changed. The version number is at the bottom right. After reloading the page you have the new version.

On layerling.com and on other web servers an open page notices an update by itself. It asks the server for its version now and then, when you come back to the tab, and at once if a program file it needs has disappeared. When something new was installed in the meantime, a card at the bottom right says so and lists what is new. “Kaydet ve yeniden yükle” writes the design you have open into the browser first and then loads the page again; the design comes back as you left it. “Sonra” holds the card back for 15 minutes. Reload soon: a page that stays on the old version may load parts of the new one that do not fit. The same card appears when that has already happened: the CAD workers, which load only when you first need them, say which build they are from, and if it is not the page's own - after an update, or with a stored copy of an older version - the card asks for a reload before the two misunderstand each other.

When layerling is open in several tabs, they look out for each other: if another tab already runs a newer version, a note at the bottom of the old tab asks you to reload it. And if the same design is open in two tabs, both warn you, because they save automatically and would overwrite each other. If you open layerling in one more tab while one is already open, the new tab suggests carrying on in the old one and offers to close itself. If you want two tabs on purpose, say for two designs side by side, click “Burada çalışmaya devam et” there. This guide opens in a tab of its own as well: while layerling is open next to it, its button at the top right reads "Back to the editor" and closes the guide instead of opening the editor a second time.

Language and appearance

You choose the language at the top right, from the language list. The colour scheme beside it offers “Sistem” (follows the operating system), “Açık”, “Koyu” and “Grafit”, a neutral dark grey.

Running it yourself

layerling is free software (AGPL-3.0) and can be run on your own computer or server, for example in a workshop, a club or a school. There are several ways, described in the README on GitHub:

  • The quick start on Windows: A single line in PowerShell installs everything and puts a shortcut on the desktop. When layerling is already running, another double-click starts no second server and only opens the page.
  • Docker: For NAS devices and home servers, without Node.js needing to be installed. Every release comes as a ready-made image henmedia/layerling on Docker Hub (also ghcr.io/henmedia/layerling) for amd64 and arm64; docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -v layerling-thumbnails:/app/.codex/project-thumbnails henmedia/layerling:latest starts it, and on a NAS you search for it in the container manager's registry. The volume layerling-thumbnails keeps the preview pictures of the start page through an update; without it they are missing each time the container is created again, until you open the design.
  • Static export: The result is plain files that any web server can serve. They belong at the root of an address (https://layerling.example.com/ or http://192.168.0.5:8080/), not in a subfolder and not opened from disk; the README has the steps. With a writable folder store next to index.html and PHP on the server it also becomes the shared storage for designs.

The MCP bridge for AI assistants exists only in the development server, see Building with an AI.

Help and feedback

  • In the editor, the “Yardım” area holds the “Kısa kılavuz” with the most important moves and the overview of keyboard shortcuts. Each section of the quick guide has a question mark that leads to the matching chapter here.
  • Questions, wishes and bug reports are welcome in the forum and on GitHub.
  • What changed in which version is in the release notes, which you find at the bottom of the start page and of the editor.

16. Videos about layerling

Videos that other people have made about layerling.

Bu bölüm henüz Türkçeye çevrilmedi. Aşağıda İngilizce metin var.

Made by others

These videos are not from this project. The links open YouTube in a new tab; nothing is loaded from there until you click.

  • Layerling Tutorials – HL ModTech (English). A playlist by a Tinkercad user, so far with a look at layerling of about 23 minutes (free, browser-based CAD that extends Tinkercad), a deeper dive into its features and a short update on printed threads.
  • Layerling – Playlist – Making Layers (English). A series about layerling, so far with "Tinkercad alternative / upgrade? Introducing Layerling!", an overview for people coming from Tinkercad, and "Layerling Sketch Tools!" on the sketch tools.
  • Layerling – TECHNOBENTO (English). A playlist about layerling, so far with “A new way to sketch in Layerling”.
  • Layerling CAD Videos – Printology (English). A playlist about layerling, so far with “I'm 100% In on Layerling - The Next Big Free CAD” and “Layerling Features That Blow Tinkercad Out Of The Water”.
  • I Tried Layerling After Tinkercad… Is It REALLY Better? – Maker Mates Studio 3D Printing (English). Someone coming from Tinkercad tries layerling and compares the two.
  • Print by Layer – Print N Repeat (English). A playlist about layerling, so far with “The EASIEST Way to Design Hinges in Layerling” and “The EASIEST Way to 3D Model Threads!”.
  • Tinkercad Too Basic? Fusion 360 Too Much? Meet Layerling for 3D Printing – 3D Jesus | 3D Printing & Design (English). A first test of layerling without any manual: fillets and chamfers, hollowing, threads, sketches, revolved bodies, patterns, import and printer profiles.
  • Layerling en español | Del primer contacto al proyecto completo – Random Maker (Spanish). A playlist in Spanish, from a first look at layerling to complete projects: how it differs from Tinkercad, a point-by-point comparison and moving projects over.
  • Proyectos en Layerling – Fulcro 1900 (Spanish). A playlist of projects in layerling, so far with an introduction to layerling as a free tool more complete than Tinkercad, desk accessories (three models), a phone case, and a threaded rod, nut and screw.
  • Layerling – Werkplaats Marc (Dutch). A playlist about layerling, so far with a first look for Tinkercad users (“Layerling - De Gratis Tussenstap van Tinkercad naar Fusion 360”) and a tutorial on sketches: tracing a photo, revolve and sweep along a path (“Schetsen Uitgelegd”).

Do you know another video, or made one yourself? Tell us in the discussions and it will be added here.

17. Tablet and touch

Working with fingers or a stylus: selecting several bodies, turning and zooming the view, the long press menu, and what to know on an iPad.

Bu bölüm henüz Türkçeye çevrilmedi. Aşağıda İngilizce metin var.

Fingers and a stylus

layerling runs in the browser of a tablet, and as an app from its home screen. A finger does what the left mouse button does. Three things a tablet does not have, a right mouse button, a Shift key and a wheel, have a way of their own:

You want toOn a tablet
Select a bodyTap it.
Select several bodiesTap a body: a round button appears in the lower left. Tap it, and every further body you tap joins the selection; a tap on a selected body takes it out again. A tap on empty space changes nothing; a second tap on the button ends it and clears the selection. Or hold a finger still for half a second, choose “Çoklu seç”, then tap one body after another.
Select all bodiesHold a finger still on empty space for half a second, choose “Tümünü seç”.
Open the menu of a right clickHold a finger still on a body or on empty space for half a second.
Move a bodyDrag it.
Resize, turn or lift a bodyDrag its handles, the small squares and arrows around it. A finger catches them from a little beside.
Turn the viewOne finger on empty space, or drag the view cube.
Zoom the viewTwo fingers: spread to come closer, pinch to go away.
Move the viewSlide two fingers together.
Clear the selectionTap empty space. Not while “Görünümü tek parmakla döndür” is on, where one finger turns the view; and in “Çoklu seç” the first tap on empty space only ends the mode and leaves the selection as it is, the next one clears it.

Selecting several bodies

Without a Shift key, “Çoklu seç” in the menu of a long press does what Shift+click does on a computer. While it is on, a message says so, and each tap on a body adds it to the selection or takes it out again. A tap on empty space, or Esc on a keyboard, ends it and leaves the selection as it is. A finger on empty space still turns the view meanwhile. Then “Grupla”, “Hizala” or a move work on all the bodies you picked.

The same menu has “Set down on a face”, the key C for a touch screen. The selection then follows the finger over the faces of other bodies; a tap sets it down on the face you tap, even a sloped one, and the first tap is enough. The menu entry is also found by searching for "set down" or "cruise" (the command search, Ctrl+K on a keyboard).

Turning and zooming the view

One finger on empty space turns the view, two fingers zoom and move it. A finger that starts on a body works on the body, not on the view. If you would rather have it turn the view, switch on “Görünümü tek parmakla döndür” in the view bar: one finger then turns the view instead of selecting, wherever it starts. That switch only shows on a device with a touch screen.

The view cube in the top left turns the view when you drag it, and a tap on one of its sides, corners or edges jumps to that view. See View and workplane.

Handles, small points and a stylus

A fingertip covers what it aims at. layerling lets a finger reach a little further to handles, points, lines and edges than a mouse pointer does, but a stylus is finer. This holds for a pen the tablet knows as a pen, such as an Apple Pencil or an S Pen. A plain stylus with a rubber tip counts as a finger for the screen and is not finer than one, so work with it as with a finger. An Apple Pencil that hovers above the screen on an iPad also shows the name of a control after a moment, in a small bubble, as the mouse pointer does with a tooltip.

In sketch mode, “Freehand” draws with the pen or a finger as on paper; when you lift it, the line becomes sketch points you can edit, see Sketches.

If bodies slip when children or hurried hands touch them, switch on “Taşımadan önce seç” in the settings: a body then has to be selected first, and only the next drag moves it.

On an iPad or iPhone

  • Install it as an app. In Safari, tap the Share icon and choose "Add to Home Screen". The app opens in a window of its own without the address bar, and it works without a connection, see Offline and install.
  • Your designs live in the browser (unless you host layerling yourself and set up a server folder). There is no account, and nothing is uploaded. Safari has a rule of its own against tracking: it deletes what a website stored after seven days in which you did not visit it in Safari. A web app added to the Home Screen is exempt from that rule, as WebKit documents it. That is one more reason to use the app from the Home Screen, and to back up important work: “Tümünü yedekle” on the start page packs all designs into one file.
  • Files. Safari lets a page write into a file only through a download, so “Dışa aktar” puts the file into the Downloads of the Files app, and Ctrl+S on a keyboard downloads it again; see Files and saving.
  • No keyboard needed. Every tool has a button in the ribbon, and a number field opens the on-screen keyboard. A keyboard on the iPad adds the keyboard shortcuts. A value box beside a body opens its number field with the second tap: the first tap only marks it, so a finger that lands on it by accident does not raise the keyboard.

Workshops with children

Fingers and rubber-tip styluses work alike here. Two settings make a class easier: “Taşımadan önce seç” so that a touch does not move a body by accident, and “Görünümü tek parmakla döndür” so that one finger always turns the view. The question mark button in the Help group of the ribbon switches on the “Etkileşimli yardım”: a tap on any button, field or handle then explains it, and the same button, or Esc, leaves it.

For a whole class, switch on “Simple mode” in the settings. The ribbon then keeps only the tools a workshop uses (copy, paste, duplicate, delete, undo, group, mirror, chamfer, fillet, hollow, align, export), the shape library a short list, the buttons are larger, and the start page shows the designs and nothing else: no news, no welcome text, no help buttons and no links out of layerling. Switching it on is a tap; switching it off is a press held for two seconds on the button that then takes its place. A link ending in ?mode=simple switches it on for the device that opens it, ?mode=full switches it off again. Whoever runs layerling on a server can start everyone in it with LAYERLING_SIMPLE_MODE=true, or fix it for everyone with always, so that the program has no switch to leave it; see the README.
